parsed.why: The felony provisions create conditional exposure for a trans woman read as male who has sex with a man, but they are not trans-specific and the latest documented enforcement finding reported no prosecutions. Social conditions and current enforcement remain uncertain.

Laws criminalise transgender depiction and gender-reassignment propaganda; recent detentions include trans people, with reported custody abuse and police violence. State propaganda and hostility, plus threats to expel foreign LGBT attendees, make discovery exceptionally dangerous.

Current rules and guidance create recurring exposure in facilities, searches and custody based on biological sex; a reported hospital case adds serious care risk. Some protections remain, but the operative restrictions and uneven regional practice dominate.

Anti-discrimination and hate-crime protections are in force, but enforcement is slow and attitudes discourage public LGBT visibility. A community group logged trans-directed violence, though the raw count has no denominator and does not establish a rate.

The seven-year same-sex-conduct offence has been applied to foreign nationals through detention and deportation; detention conditions and state hostility heighten the consequences. The record does not establish a trans-specific offence or current enforcement frequency.
